description: Count your steps for 30 seconds to get steps per minute and a rating against the 170–180 target.

faqs.a: Many coaches target 170–180 steps per minute for efficient distance running; sprinters go higher, walkers lower.
Count every footstrike for 30 seconds and double it. Count one foot and multiply by 4 also works.
Slightly — a quicker, lighter cadence usually means shorter strides and lower impact per step.

howto: Count every step you take in 30 seconds.
See your steps/min and how it rates vs 170–180.
title: Running Cadence Calculator
